## Cross validation
Randomly split you data into training and testing 
- The training data you use to build your model
- Testing is date you use to evaluate out of dampl fit
- Exact ratio depends on data sixe, but I like 80/20
- Evaluate using the root mean squared error (compute it only in the testing data set)
- What a higher RMSE

Repeat the partition a couple of times 
You can fold (5-fold is where the data is split into 5 parts. One is training and the other 4 are test)

Comes up a lot in modern methods
- variable selection (lasso)
- most of the time you don't really get p-values, you focus on prediction accuracy instead 
- its because the goals are usually different for these types of analysis. 


# Coding


### load in packages 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(mgcv)
library(p8105.datasets)
```



## Lidar data
```{r}
data("lidar")

lidar_df =
  lidar |> 
  mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
  select(id, everything()) #this reoders things to put id in the front

lidar_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x= range, y = logratio)) +
  geom_point()

```
Build training and testing datasets - sample at random your training data set 

```{r}
train_df = sample_frac(lidar_df, size = .8)
test_df = anti_join(lidar_df, train_df, by = "id") #of everything in one thing, what is not in the other
```

```{r}
ggplot(train_df, aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_point(data = test_df, color = "red") #you can see where the testing data set in red 
```


Fit some models 
```{r}
linear_mod = lm(logratio ~ range, data = train_df)
smooth_mod = mgcv::gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = train_df) #gam stands for generalized additive models, s stands for a smooth fit, but gam does still assume constant variance - Jeff hates cubic polynomials lol 
wiggly_mod = mgcv::gam(logratio ~ s(range, k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = train_df) #this happens when you add a number of breaks 
```

make a plot
```{r}
train_df |> 
  add_predictions(wiggly_mod) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")

```
do model comparisons 
```{r}
rmse(linear_mod, test_df)
rmse(smooth_mod, test_df)
rmse(wiggly_mod, test_df)
```
